It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

It is the cry that silenced them and the earthquake that made them still. Qatadah said this: "The overwhelming blast is the cry." This is also the preference of Ibn Jarir [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/31).]].

Mujahid said: "The overwhelming blast is the sins." Likewise al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Ibn Zayd said: it is the transgression. Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿Thamud denied by its transgression﴾ [al-Shams: 11].

As-Suddi said regarding ﴿they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast﴾: he meant the slayer of the she-camel.

﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind﴾, that is, a cold one. Qatadah, al-Rabi', as-Suddi and ath-Thawri said: ﴿raging﴾ means extremely strong in its blowing. Qatadah said: it raged over them until it pierced their hearts.

Ad-Dahhak said: ﴿furious﴾ means cold, ﴿raging﴾ means it raged over them without mercy or blessing. Ali and others said: it raged over the keepers (the treasurers of the winds), so it came out without measure.

﴿He subjected it against them﴾, that is, He let it prevail over them, ﴿for seven nights and eight days in succession﴾, that is: complete, consecutive, ominous.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, ath-Thawri and others said: ﴿in succession﴾ means consecutive.

From Ikrimah and al-Rabi': ominous upon them, like His saying: ﴿in ominous days﴾ [Fussilat: 16]. Al-Rabi' said: the first of them was a Friday. Others said a Wednesday. It is said that they are the days people call al-A'jaz (the Final Days of the Month), and it seems people took this from His saying: ﴿So you see the people in it fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees﴾. It is also said that they occur at the end of winter, and it is called the days of the old woman, because an old woman from the people of 'Ad entered a cave, and the wind killed her on the eighth day. This was related by al-Baghawi [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (208).]], and Allah knows best.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿hollow﴾ means ruined. Others said: decayed, meaning the wind would strike one of them against the ground, and he would fall dead upon the top of his head, his skull would be crushed, and his body would remain lifeless, as if it were the trunk of a palm tree when it falls without branches.

It passed by the people of the desert, carrying them, their livestock and their wealth, and placed them between the sky and the earth. When the people of the settled areas saw the wind and what was in it, they said: 'This is a cloud that will bring us rain.' Then it cast the people of the desert and their livestock upon the people of the settled areas" [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/421) and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah no. (806), through Muhammad ibn Fudayl from Muslim, with the same. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/113): "In it is Muslim al-Mala'i, who is weak."]].

﴿So do you see for them any remnant?﴾, that is: do you perceive any one of their survivors who is attributed to them? Rather, they were eradicated to the last of them, and Allah did not make for them any successor.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿attentive﴾ means retentive and hearing. Qatadah said: ﴿an attentive ear﴾ means one that comprehended from Allah and benefited from what it heard of the Book of Allah. Ad-Dahhak said: ﴿and that an attentive ear may retain it﴾, an ear heard it and retained it. That is: whoever has sound hearing and sound reason. This is general for whoever understands and retains.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Subh al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Zayd ibn Yahya narrated to us, Ali ibn Hawshab narrated to us, I heard Makhul saying: When this was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿and that an attentive ear may retain it﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I asked my Lord to make it the ear of Ali." [Makhul said:] So Ali would say: "I never heard anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and forgot it."

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Amir narrated to us, Bishr ibn Adam narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr Abu Muhammad, father of Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, narrated to us, Salih ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, I heard Buraydah al-Aslami say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ali: "I have been commanded to bring you near and not to distance you, and to teach you and that you should retain, and it is right for you to retain." He said: So this verse was revealed: ﴿and that an attentive ear may retain it﴾.

Ibn Jarir related it from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from Bishr ibn Adam, with it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/36). Ibn Asakir related it in Tarikh Dimashq, as in al-Kanz no. (36426), and Ibn Asakir said: "This isnad is unknown and the hadith is shadhdh."]]. Then Ibn Jarir related it through another route from Dawud al-A'ma, from Buraydah, with it. Commentary of the Exegesis of Surah al-Haqqah

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Al-Haqqah (the Inevitable Reality) is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, because in it the promise and the threat are realized. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, magnified its matter, saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?﴾

Then Allah, exalted is He, mentioned His destruction of the nations that denied it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast﴾. It is the cry that silenced them and the earthquake that made them still. Qatadah said this: "The overwhelming blast is the cry." This is also the preference of Ibn Jarir [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/31).]].

Mujahid said: "The overwhelming blast is the sins." Likewise al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Ibn Zayd said: it is the transgression. Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿Thamud denied by its transgression﴾ [al-Shams: 11].

As-Suddi said regarding ﴿they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast﴾: he meant the slayer of the she-camel.

﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind﴾, that is, a cold one. Qatadah, al-Rabi', as-Suddi and ath-Thawri said: ﴿raging﴾ means extremely strong in its blowing. Qatadah said: it raged over them until it pierced their hearts.

Ad-Dahhak said: ﴿furious﴾ means cold, ﴿raging﴾ means it raged over them without mercy or blessing. Ali and others said: it raged over the keepers (the treasurers of the winds), so it came out without measure.

﴿He subjected it against them﴾, that is, He let it prevail over them, ﴿for seven nights and eight days in succession﴾, that is: complete, consecutive, ominous.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, ath-Thawri and others said: ﴿in succession﴾ means consecutive.

From Ikrimah and al-Rabi': ominous upon them, like His saying: ﴿in ominous days﴾ [Fussilat: 16]. Al-Rabi' said: the first of them was a Friday. Others said a Wednesday. It is said that they are the days people call al-A'jaz (the Final Days of the Month), and it seems people took this from His saying: ﴿So you see the people in it fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees﴾. It is also said that they occur at the end of winter, and it is called the days of the old woman, because an old woman from the people of 'Ad entered a cave, and the wind killed her on the eighth day. This was related by al-Baghawi [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (208).]], and Allah knows best.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿hollow﴾ means ruined. Others said: decayed, meaning the wind would strike one of them against the ground, and he would fall dead upon the top of his head, his skull would be crushed, and his body would remain lifeless, as if it were the trunk of a palm tree when it falls without branches.

It is established in the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "I was helped by the east wind, and 'Ad were destroyed by the west wind" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1035) and Sahih Muslim no. (900).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn al-Durays al-'Abdi narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Muslim, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah did not open upon 'Ad from the wind with which they were destroyed except the amount of the opening of a ring. It passed by the people of the desert, carrying them, their livestock and their wealth, and placed them between the sky and the earth. When the people of the settled areas saw the wind and what was in it, they said: 'This is a cloud that will bring us rain.' Then it cast the people of the desert and their livestock upon the people of the settled areas" [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/421) and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah no. (806), through Muhammad ibn Fudayl from Muslim, with the same. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/113): "In it is Muslim al-Mala'i, who is weak."]].

ath-Thawri narrated from Layth, from Mujahid: the wind has two wings and a tail.

﴿So do you see for them any remnant?﴾, that is: do you perceive any one of their survivors who is attributed to them? Rather, they were eradicated to the last of them, and Allah did not make for them any successor.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 69, verse 25–37:

This is an account of the state of the wretched when one of them is given his record in the place of gathering (al-'Arasat) in his left hand. At that point he will regret with the utmost regret, and he will say: ﴿But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record, and had not known what my account is. Oh, I wish it had been the end."﴾

Ad-Dahhak said: It means a death after which there is no life. Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Rabi' and as-Suddi said the same.

Qatadah said: He wishes for death, and there was nothing in the world more hateful to him than it.

﴿My wealth has not availed me. My authority has passed away from me.﴾ That is: my wealth and my status did not repel from me the punishment and the might of Allah; rather, the matter has come down to me alone, so there is no helper for me and no protector. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Seize him and shackle him. Then burn him in Hellfire.﴾

That is: He commands the angels of punishment (az-Zabaniyah) to seize him violently from the place of gathering and shackle him, meaning they place the chains around his neck, then bring him to Hell and cause him to burn in it, meaning they immerse him in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says ﴿Seize him,﴾ seventy thousand angels will rush to him; each angel among them will say, "Like this," and will cast seventy thousand into the Fire.

Ibn Abi ad-Dunya related in "al-Ahwal": that four hundred thousand will rush to him, and nothing will be left that he does not crush. He will say, "What is between me and you?" It will say, "Indeed, the Lord is angry with you, and everything is angry with you."

Al-Fudayl (that is, ibn 'Iyad) said: When the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says ﴿Seize him and shackle him,﴾ seventy thousand angels will rush to him, each of them wanting to be the one who places the shackle on his neck.

﴿Then burn him in Hellfire﴾ meaning: immerse him in it.

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us﴾, meaning: if Muhammad (ﷺ) had been, as they claim, one who invents lies against Us, so that he added to the message or subtracted from it, or said something from himself and attributed it to Us, when that is not the case, We would have hastened to punish him. For this reason He said: ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾. It was said that its meaning is: We would have taken vengeance on him with the right hand, because it is stronger in striking. It was also said: We would have seized him by his right hand.

﴿Then We would have cut off from him the aorta﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the *niyat al-qalb* (the sinews of the heart), which is the vein to which the heart is attached. Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hakam, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Muslim al-Batin, and Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: it is the heart, its membranes, and what is adjacent to it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So none of you could withhold Us from him﴾, meaning: none of you could prevent between Us and him if We intended some such thing against him. The meaning in this is (in M: "in that"): rather, he is truthful, righteous, and rightly guided, because God, mighty and majestic, confirms for him what he conveys from Him, and supports him with the manifest miracles (in M: "the overpowering") and the decisive proofs.

Then He said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for the God-fearing﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, as He said: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe a guidance and a healing; but as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

Then He said (in M: "as He said") ﴿And indeed, We know that among you are deniers﴾, meaning: despite this clarity and explicitness, there will be among you those who deny the Qur'an.

Then He said: ﴿And indeed, it is a regret for the disbelievers﴾. Ibn Jarir said: indeed, denial is a regret for the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, and he related the same from Qatadah.

Ibn Abi Hatim related, through the chain of al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿And indeed, it is a regret for the disbelievers﴾, meaning: a remorse. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, meaning: indeed, the Qur'an and faith in it are, in reality, a regret for the disbelievers, as He said: ﴿Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in it﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 200–201], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ [Saba': 54]. For this reason He said here: ﴿And indeed, it is the truth of certainty﴾, i.e., the true, certain report in which there is no doubt, no uncertainty, and no suspicion.

Then He said: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾, i.e., the One who sent down this great Qur'an.

[End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Haqqah", and all praise is due to God (in A: "and all praise, grace, thanks, and beautiful praise are due to God"). ] [Addition from M, A.]
